methodology: Same disposable repositories and selected patch; actual PTY screen markers. First process run excluded from warm medians; four warm runs with rotated client order. No OS cache flush. HEAD and staged changes verified after every client. RSS is parent-only at patch visibility, not peak memory or completed background highlighting.

sidecar.startup_scope: Engine spawn and protocol handshake only; excludes Node module loading and validator compilation.
sidecar.methodology: Persistent release engine through generated Node client. No rendering or models. Git Trace2 enabled for process counts. Native Git is a subprocess baseline, not another app. Samples run on a shared development machine; not a universal ranking.

source_install_check.profile: release, thin LTO, one codegen unit, symbols stripped
checks: Real PTY staging and commit smoke

comparison_backend.working_status: asyncgit uses gix 0.75 for index/worktree status; confirmed in its source, not inferred from timings

capture_probe.methodology: Single read-only working-tree capture, not a latency distribution. Trace2 counts subprocesses. Reveals per-file patch-process overhead; do not extrapolate timing linearly.

before_observation.duration: Reported as minutes; no precise before timing recorded

large_staged_capture_after_fix.scope: One local staged-capture run. Same selected-file count and patch size as the report. No model inference. Request estimates are not actual provider usage.

compare_rpc_after_cache_fix.scope: Measures the Compare RPC used by Mako, not rendering. Other phases in this run were much slower than the earlier baseline, including native Git. Status-cache TTL expired during the run; do not present all phases as cache hits or infer a fresh-status speedup.

status_trace_observation.scope: One saved Trace2 status sample, not an aggregate.

limitations: No live-provider semantic accuracy or cost comparison
No peak-memory or total process-tree memory comparison
GitUI remains faster for startup to visible patch in this fixture
